                                  EOITOR!AL
        Recently we have received comments from several pro-UFO readers
 questioning the relevancy and value or what we have published in the last
 couple of years. We have apparently not been pro-ET enough. A clarification
 is in order.
        While we may personally think that there is something very worthwhile
 and unexplained about some UFO reports, organizationally our purpose is not
 to advocate an answer, pro or con, without harder information. We are fill-
 ing historical gaps in the record, publishing what we hope is interesting,
 original research, and, of course, trying to put an end to secrecy relating
 to UFO reports. Our purpose is not to force •spins" on information that we
 obtain in order to satisfy the beliefs or pro or con UFO researchers. If
 UFO information is censored or withheld, it does not mean that such inform-
 ation is de racto proof or an answer to UFOs. Nor does it mean that such
 information is therefore unimportant and not related to UFOs but to other
 security concerns. !t does mean that UFO information is being withheld con-
 trary to the conclusions or the government's Condon Report, the official
 document which ended the Air force's involvement in the public UFO debate.
 The report concluded that the study of UFOs could not be expected to advance
 science and that no hazard or threat to national security existed. If so,
 then the secrecy makes no sense and all •lthheld UFO data should be •ade
 available.                                                              .
        We could very likely double our subscription rolls by report>ng
 tittilating stories of underground allen bases, of simple verbal accounts        ,
 clai•ing kno•ledge of UFO technology, of •hat has become so very trendy
 now _ alien/human SEXI Actually it •ould not be enough to report such in-
 ror•ation _ •e would have to advocate it on a soapbox. T~en •e •ould llkely
 be invited onto numerous media progra•s to give the publ1c •hat lt craves -
 sensation.
        As one UFO pundit told us recently, printing sens ibl e 1 n f orma tlon
 is not the road to fame and fortune. Tryslngbet~tbew~a!:~;~dt~n1n~~~=~u~ot
 seem to be undesirable traits to some. o        ·
 to put on a Wild-West show.

                   THE ESTIMATE OF THE SITUATION
       Readers of UFO history will at one time or another have come across
mention of an Air Force document called the "Estimate of the Situation.•
"Estimates" were prepared by the Air Force during the early years of the
UFO controversy to cover a wide variety or topics, most of which were not
UFO-related. However, one was prepared in 1948, according to former Project
Blue Book head, Captain Edward Ruppelt, addressing the issue of flying
saucers. Ruppelt said that if one had something to say about a vital issue,
an Estimate was written.
       The document ~as said to be a thick document with a black cover,
printed on legal-sized paper. It was stamped "Top Secret.• Written some-
time in mid-1948, shortly after the famous Chiles/Whitted saucer Incident
or July 24, 1948, over Alabama, the authors of the report (personnel at
Project Sign, the Air Force's first official UFO study) had concluded that
after a year of study flying saucers were interplanetary . The Estimate
was sent on its way upwards through the chain of command for inspection.
It was eventually rejected by the Air Force Chief of Staff, General Hoyt
Vandenberg. Vandenberg declared that the report lacked proof and ordered
it declassified and destroyed. Reportedly, a copy of the Estimate sur~i~ed
until at least 1952, •hen it was seen by both Ruppelt and Major Dewey
Fournet, the Air Force's Project Monitor for Blue Book, the Air Force's
most •ell-kno•n incarnation of UFO investigation.
       With these two named individuals the only ones identifiable who had
seen the document outside of the original official line of con~and, they
were the best source or post-1948 information about the Estimate. Ruppelt
died in 1960, but Fournet is still living and was recently interviewed
about the Estimate by CAUS associate, Jim Melesciuc.
       Fournet explained that the report was discovered in the files that
he had inherited as the Air Force's UFO project monitor at the Pentagon.
He had virtually stumbled across it •hile researching other UFO background
•aterial.
       The report, he said, was not especially thick, •aybe 20-30 pages,
and it still had the security marking on it, though it •as supposed to
have been declassified. It reviewed all or the apparently unexplained
reports received by the Air Force up to the time the Estimate was written.
Logical explanations were explored for the cases used, but in the end the
extraterrestrial explanation was regarded as the answer. Fournet was very
explicit in stating that the Estimate contained no confirmation of artifacts
having been recovered from flying saucers.
       There was according to Fournet's recollection, deplorably little
UFO sighting data available when the report ~as written, and that the
extraterrestrial conclusion was the result or "extreme extrapolation."
It wa s felt that the Esti•ate's purpose was to create enough interest in
Air Force Intelligence with such a premature conclusion so as to •otivate

     My article was based on a careful study of the writings
of UFO abduction specialists, with particular attention to
numerical data. That data is scanty, and applies only to
the United States, the locale of 99% of abduction research.
Theoretically, abductions might be a global phenomenon, but
1 am forced to work with the facts at hand, not speculation
about how many Chinese or Sudanese abductees exist.
     When mathematical analysis of those numbers is applied,
the result is indeed ''preposterous.'' In fact, I began my
study as a a debunking exercise, convinced that analysis
would show that abductions could not possibly be physical
events. I will grant Dennis Stacy that ''figures lie and
liars figure,'' but wish he would attack the logic and data
that was employed, rather than the conclusion, unpalatable
though it may be.
     An aspect of my analysis that seems difficult to convey
is that it does not rely on raw total numbers so much as it
does on the rate at which the abduction events occur. If
you see the big sign in Detroit listing how many cars have
been built this year, it will seem impossible. But then
vhen you consider how many workers in how many plants are
•aking those cars, three shifts per day, it begins to make
sense.
     On the other hand, if we relied entirely on math, we
would have to close our eyes every time a bumblebee buzzed
by, because the aerodynamic engineers long since ''proved''
that it can't fly!
     My personal view is that abductions are probably not
physical events, but I base that opinion on the lack of
physical evidence and eyewitness testimony.
     Stacy makes some excellent points. I hope that UFO
researchers will pursue the logic that both of us have
employed, using it as a fresh way to study abductions, which
are surely one of the most profound mysteries of our time.

that HUFOX UFO JOURNAL, last full paragraph of the first column. I do have the option to
ask the field invest.igator (s) for additional information on any report T deem to be missing

based on infonaation quality, strangeness, and witne~s reliability along the lines recom-
mended by Ballester and Cuasp in "Standards in the Evaluation of UFO Reports" (1981, in The
SpectrUia of UFO Research, CUFOS 1988). The "information quality" factor depends on the

~riting stri.ctly as~? editor Wan author, the pro~lems with this article begin with its title:
 D1sappeanng Enhhes, Techrucally-Controlled L1fe Forms, Alternative Realities and Other
Bizarre Machines Operated by the UFO Intelligences" From your point of view-and from mine
too, for that matter-it's an ambitious undertaking. In fact, it would make a good chapter in a '
book

From th~ standpoint of most UFO journal editors, however, myself included, it's s1mply too long
and ~nw1eldly to accommodate wtth?ut a great expend1ture of personal time and energy, either to
rewnte large chunks or ruthlessly ed1t the whole (or both) In other words, preparing it for
publication in the Journal represents a major undertaking on my pan. I've just done same with a
shorter article by half submitted by Victoria Lacas/Aiexander, so I know whereof! speak. You
yourself divide the piece into three sections, which is some indication, at approximately 8000
words, ofjust how long the article is The only editor I can think of who tmght accept it
reasonably uncut at this length is Gordon Creighton ofFlymg Saucer Rem~w

Although generally well written, there ace a number of stylistic habits displayed which tend to
drive editors crazy Repetition is one, overall wordiness is another. Here is a relatively innocuous,
but all too common, example Early on you write that "The man did not respond when Mr. B
spoke to him, and he walked away when Mr. B walked towacd him." An editor would rewrite
this something along the lines of"The man did not respond when Mr. B. spoke to him, and
walked away as he approached " Your sentence has 21 words, mine 17 Admittedly, that probably
doesn't sound like a vast improvement, but over the length of an 8000-word manuscript it
amounts to roughly one-fifth fewer words, or about 1600 words

Here's another example of repetition "But that was not the purpose for visiting Mr B or Dr
I Iopkins. The purpose fQr visiting Mr B and Dr. Hopkins was to perform psychological
experiments on human beings" All of the underlined words are essentially repetitious. In another
instance you use the phrase "in key cases described in this article" in two consecutive, short
paragraphs. In another smgle short paragraph, you use the word "vanishing" six times in a mere
three sentences Does the word prolix mean anything?

You also use phrases like "this article takes up" and even "That is what this article is about ." Why
have to tell the reader what an article is about? Just write the damn thing

NEW EXAM

Whoever among you and your members haven't yet taken the field investigator's
exam1natton should do so quickly. I put 1t together over a decade ago and, rev1ewing it
recently. realized 1t was senously out of date Too many of the quesbons asked for
answers from UFO ·pnmers· (such as J Allen Hynek's seminal work) that are nonethe-
less far out of pnnt at this point, while the fourth ed1tion of the F1eld Investigator's
Manual offers a wealth of new matenal. Why then should members try to pass the
original exam now? Because the new exam is at once more fair and qu1te a b1t more
difficult, with the same 80 percent as a passing grade.

In all, 46 of the original exam's quest1ons have been replaced, while several more were
updated Every answer in the new version can be obta1ned from the latest manual (but
you'll have to dig), from a dictionary or from direct observabon of the sky. It"s been
submitted to the Board of Directors for approval and will probably take effect 1n the
coming months.

So that you know, there was an ulterior motive in redesigning the exam. For too long
too many members have been able to slide by w1thout knowledge of 1nvest1gattve
basics, and that has translated to poorly prepared case reports. In a word, no one can
pass the new exam without a fairly thorough knowledge of the manual's contents.
Which is as it should be. Computer programmers cannot devise programs without a
thorough under-standing of computer languages. Police detectives, teachers, lawyers,
forest rangers and a host of other professionals must pass rigorous exams to be
certified. It should be no different for our para-professional investigators

simply must purchase a manual from Seguin and really study it Then, when they pass

    COPIES TO: MUFON Board of Directors and David Spencer

    SUBJECT:               Revised (June 1993) Procedures and Routing of Investiga-
                           tion Reports for Evaluation (USA and Canada)
    This letter supersedes the letter of 10 May 1991 which provided
    directions for routing of reports during the period when the post
    of MUFON Deputy Director of Investigations was vacant.        These
    revised procedures seek to streamline the report processing
    sequence between the Field Investigators and Headquarters, without
    bypassing the important steps of inspection and review at the
    levels of Section, State and Regional Directors; alao to relieve an
    expensive and unwarranted burden of copying and mailing coats from
    the shoulders of the Field Investigators, who already volunteer
    much of their time and out-of-pocket expenses in the effort to
    investigate the cases and write the reports. Finally, it should
    eliminate the problem of multiple copies of the same report, some
    with added or deleted data, arriving at different times in the
    office of the Deputy Director, Investigation, for final processing
    and computer entry, the sorting-out of which requires an added
    drain on that volunteer's limited time and resources.

     Case Assignment
     Upon initial receipt of information regarding a claimed UFO
     sighting (through the International Director, a public agen~y, the
     news media, contacts to the State Section Director, State D1rec~or
     or elsewhere ) the case should be referred to the State Se7t1.on
     Director resp~nsible for the county in which the witness r!sl.~esi
     The State Section Director should immediately contac t the pr. ~Cl.i~e
     reporting witness (usually via telephone ) in o rder to verl Y. ts
     reported information and determine whether suffi cient reason eus
     to warrant a formal investigation.

assigned to the investigation, the State Director must be advised

investigation and report .
In moat case circumstances likely to involve a detailed account, it
is far preferable to assign two persona (e.g. a Section Direc-
tor/Field Investigator and Trainee), at least one of whom has
con•iderable investigative experience. During the witness inter-
view(•) and otherwise, two investigators working together tend to
gather more and clearer evidence.
CAte Monitoring
Often, UFO claims can soon be resolved as misidentifications of
celestial objects, conventional aircraft and other mundane stimuli
(IFOs), at which point it is unnecessary to continue . However,
when the circumstances warrant a thorough examination, the State
Director (or Chief Investigator) must ensure continued progress
toward a resolution, offering insights and logistical support as
necessary. If an unnecessary delay is perceived, a reassignment
should be considered.
Case Report Submittal
After review and determination that the case report is both clear
and complete, it should be submitted in the following manner.
     - Send the original materials comprising the case record to
the State Section Director, if that person was responsible for the
assignment and monitoring of the case, but not directly invo~ved
with the investigation and writing of the report . . Otherwl.se,
original materials should go directly to the State D1.rector, who
may wish to make and retain photocopies for s~ate files. If the

materials may pass through both State D1.re~tors off1.ces as agreed
to by communication between thosa State D1.rectors.

Case Report Evaluation and Feedback
The Regional Director reviews the entire case record .      After
assigning a log number, he/she prepares a "Preliminary Evaluation
of a UFO Report."    Based upon all case factors and any other
information known at the time, the case report is assessed as:
     (a)  complete for evaluation purposes and thereby graded in
     terms of its verifications and importance to UFOlogy;
     (b) resolved in respect to a known or probable occurrence in
     the same geographic area and timeframe (e .g. re-entry of space
     debris); or
     (c) incomplete for evaluation purposes due to case factors
     that are unclear are not addressed, or conflict. (Note: An
     evaluation of "i~complete" does not imply that the event. never
     occurred. Rather, it is to state that the case report J.tself
     does not firmly support a UFO conclusion.)
                                    3
The •Preliminary Evaluation• page becomes a cover page attached to
the front of the report, and the package is sent either forward to
the Deputy Director of Investigations, or held for additional
information or clarification from the Field Investigator(s). When
the Regional Director's requirements for completeness are met or
it is clear that no further data will be forthcoming on that c~se
the Regional Director sends the original report materials (retain:
ing copies of all, part or none as desired) to MUFON • s Deputy
Director of Investigations for final processing, computer database
entry, and archive filing at HUFON Headquarters.

    The witness exited the car after parking and noted few other cars in the lot and no other persons.
    He then looked off to the northwestern horizon and saw a line of red lights in the distance. The
    lights slowly pulsed off to bright in unison and gave him the impression of radio towers in the
    distance.

    Witness then noticed that the lights were slowly moving together in a straight-line southeast
    toward the theater. This brought the lights parallel to the witness just above the treeline at the
    edge of the parking lot. As the lights approached, it seemed to the witness that lights were part
    of one object which was confirmed as the object approached.

    In a personal interview with the investigator, the witness described the object as a large disk
    approximately I 00 yards in diameter. silver-gray metallic color 111ith a line of slowly pulsing red
    lights around the body of the disk. Witness estimated the size d•sk based on distance covered

    circles visible. The witness' impression was that the circles were portholes.

    As the object approached, the reporting witness' female companion got out of the car and asked
    "What are you looking at?" lbe witness rcplicd,"U1at over there·•. The companion then asked
    "'What is it?'' in an astonished tone. She did not speak during the rest of the event or talk about
    the event at a later time. The \vitness stated she was uncomfortable '' 1th the subject.

    Witness reports that the disk drifted slowly toward the lot until II was at the edge_ of the treeline
    and the lot. It hovered above the trees approximately 250-275 yards from the '~1messes ''ho
    then had an unobstructed view of the disk. At this point , wimess stated the disk made a quick
    movement "lurched" faster than he was able to follow. The \vitness reported that it performed
    this maneuver once and only traveled a few feet to the left.

    Witness states that disk hovered for a few moments, then drifted over the tree~ to t~e west out of
    sight. Witness reported that the disk then reappeared within a few mmutes at us pomt of ongtn.
    northwest of the theater lot and began to approach the theater a second time along the same path.

changed dtrcctlon, dri~ted .west over lhe trees and did not reappear. The witness did not see any
other patrons at the dnvc-m theater who witnesses !he event.

Notes from telephone call 3(2/96, from Barbara, age 50s

At first I'd tum on the radio to drwon out the hum, but then I got used to the
hum, and I started to look forward to it. and finally I embraced it.

I'd send messages to the energy that I didn't mind them experimenting or
checking me out as long as they didn't hurt me.

I don't know how you get chosen. There is an energy around paper, and I
could put a flat piece of papger under my arm and take it out and it would
be creased. It began by my noticing creases on brand new books. I
mentioned this to a co-worker and he showed me creased paper in his
wallet; he thought his wife was doing it. He'd bought several new wallets
because of it. One day I got the Post [newspaper] and it was folded
like an accordion.

Certain people are coded, tho I can never decipher the coding. and
certain people are sent messages through the coding. I think I am coded.
I've never discussed this with anybody. I notice something going on with
me but it's not negative cause if it were I wouldn't be here. I also found
splashes of color on my clothing and I tought someone was trying to get in
touch with me.

I was intensely interested in metaphysics and I came home and just before
I flicked on the light switch, I saw a royal blue triangle over my dresser. I
was drawn to go to the dresser and this thing passed through me.

I feel my kids are being contacted. I'd see the same yellow splashes on
their clothing and I also saw it on my kitchen floor.

My husband turned strongly toward Christianity and I get the feeling
something's going on with him, but I don't think it's anything bad.

A while back I read Communion.

I attribute my clean lifestyle (no meat) to them, and my concern f~r th~
planet. I feel our thoughts and actions are what keeps the planet m A- .
condition. I buy environmentally friendly producs, and they have me gomg

all over looking for natural fibres so my body Will be chemically
independe~t. .People come up to me and ask, Are you religious? because
you look rehg1ous. I'm not religious. I believe there's something in addition
to the Bible.

My sister believes in UFOs. She looks up in the sky for UFOs and she
watches Sightings.

My oldest son is different from his father. His father's position is he's in
control and there's nothing going on that he doesn't know about. I asked
him if he has the ringing in his ear and he [denied vehemently].

I feel th energy is giving the US government technology and I feel some US
govt officials are showing them certain people who they can use. How do
you think we got lasers?

MARKS ON YOUR BODY? Needle marks.

Sometimes late at night I do get information about things they are
experimenting with.

 Brunch Meetin'i
 Following the two-hour telecast, "UFO Cover-Up? ... Live,·· the

National Board member Richard lluines noted lhat the UFO question
ie becoming a new eocia~ mo~ement which m~y be threatening to the
public. ··we face an ep~dem~c of in!ormat1on, ·· he said, in reference

Dr . Rema Laibow said there is a need for meetings of psychiatrists

As the first--and only--organization dedicated to supporting
scientific research into all aspects of the phenomenon, the
Fund for UFO Research has emerged as a leader in the field.
Now in its lOth year, the Fund has an outstanding list of
accomplishments:
      * Sci entific Research--The Fund has awarded more than
            20 grants to support scientific research into case
            investigations, historical documentation and
            photographic analyses.
      * Public Education--The Fund has sponsored
           conferences and symposia, conducted an aggressive
           media relations campaign and cooperated in an
           ongoing program to educate scientists and
           congressional leaders about the importance of the
           UFO question.
      * Fundraising--Since it was organized in 1979, the
           Fund has raised more than $150,000 from private
           citizens like yourself. Operating without an
           office or a paid staff, the organization devotes
           100% of its revenues to support scientific research
           and public education projects. We accept frQ
           government funds.

Dear Elaine:
      Thank you for showing me the manuscript on "Disappearing Entities," which
is interesting, well written, and publishable.     Unfortunately it ie not an
article suited to !UR's particular slant.
      The sorts of stories you relate are what I call (in a forthcoming book)
"extreme anomalous claims" and by their very nature unprovable. we cannot even
be sure that their relationship to the UFO phenomenon is real or siroply apparenL
IUR and CUFOS have always preferred to keep their focus on UFO-related phen~na
that are scientifically investigatable and potentially verifiable.
      I have spent a great deal of time thinking about these sorts of extreme
claims and discuss them at lenqth in my next boOk, in which I endeavor to sound
like neither a debunker nor a John Keel.
      I appreciate your thinking of IUR, and I have no doubt that you'll bo able
to place this elsewhere.

            Blett:bmao's suggestion that such a teach-in might boost show ratings. A
            college teach-in led by qualified academic and scientific experts would
            certainly be a respectable way to present the subject for examination by
            colleges across the country.

                   The three UFO organizations referenced in Mr. Bletcltman's letter are
            well recognized and have solid reputations due to their large number of

            their affiliate groups, have been involved in our current UFO research e1l'ort

Dear Elaine:

     Enclosed is a copy of my itinery for the conference in
Washington, D.C. I've also enclosed a copy of the press kit for
the book.

     As I mentioned last night, the title of my talk will be
Eyewitness to Roswell. It will feature a recording of the actual
news broadcast of July 8, 1947 and it will feature drawings
based on the eyewitness testimony of the participants. Although
Don put together the drawings, they were made as the witness sat
there an made the corrections. The speech will feature new data
about the Roswell case and will cover the story as we have been
able to reconstruct the events after forty-five years.
     I will need a slide projector and a cassette audio tape
player for the news broadcast recording. If there are microphones
for the speakers, a small cassette deck will work.
     I would appreciate a ride from the airport to the hotel and
I would appreciate it if you would book a room for me for Friday
and Saturday night .                          $ 30S' 2
     At the moment I can think of nothing else. If you have
questions or need ~nything, please let me know. Thanks for the
opportunity to speak to your group.


                yours,

                     This 1s in follow up to our telephone conversation on

                pass on to you some of my questions about the Rosvell
                incident that I hope might be of use to you in your research
                work. First, I   will give you a brief outline of my history
                and professional qualifications in order to provide some
                backdrop to my views on the events at Rosvell as reported in
                the Berlitz/Moore and Randle/Schmitt books.

I                     I am a 1965 graduate from Duke University in Math and
                Physics.  I spent the  next 26 years as a Navy Nuclear
                Submarine   officer, eventually commanding the USS JAMES
                MADISON, a fleet ballistic missile nuclear submarine. Since
                retirement, I have been with the Department of fnergy as a
                nuclear engineer and senior program manager in the test
                reactor area.  In the Navy, I had five years experience in
                the Pentagon and the Congressional arena. As a hobby, J
                have spent a lot of time in researching the origins of
                humankind, the evolution of culture and religion/mythology,
                the UFO phenomenon, and paranormal subjects in general.
                However, I would not call myself an expert in any of these
                subjects.
